currentContext.expansion: Adani Cement's installed capacity reached 109 MTPA in FY 2025-26, up from 89 MTPA, driven by the integration of strategic acquisitions (Sanghi Industries, Penna Cement) and consistent project execution; the platform targets 119 MTPA by FY 2026-27 in a phased manner through a balanced mix of greenfield and brownfield projects, with the ambition to be the lowest-cost cement manufacturer. Specific projects under way include a 1.5 MTPA capacity addition at Sindri (organic route), a 0.3 MTPA addition through debottlenecking, and 3.4 MTPA of ongoing expansion comprising 2.4 MTPA at Salai Banwa and 1 MTPA at Kalamboli. ACC's own standalone cement capacity stood at 40.4 MTPA. Alongside capacity growth, the Company is expanding captive power (315 MW installed capacity, including 86 MW of Waste Heat Recovery Systems) and pursuing rail and sea-based logistics investments (e.g. at Sanghipuram, via captive jetty) to support expansion economics. ACC and parent Ambuja Cements have also strengthened captive limestone resources to secure long-run raw-material supply for expansion.

risks.risk: Maintaining market position in a dynamic industry environment
risks.note: The Indian cement market is evolving rapidly, with consolidations and ongoing capacity additions increasing competitive pressure on market share and profitability.

risks.risk: Compliance with changes in the regulatory landscape
risks.note: Regulatory requirements are evolving rapidly in response to climate and environmental concerns; non-compliance carries reputational and financial consequences, and addressing new emission standards (dust, SOx, NOx) can involve substantial transformation costs.

The cement industry is capital-intensive and heavily reliant on energy and resources such as limestone, fly ash and coal, which constitute a significant portion of operating costs, making cost management and supply security critical.
ACC must continuously identify and mitigate potential data leakages and threats to its information systems, including risks from the expanding use of AI tools across the organisation.
Health and safety are fundamental to operations, requiring a multidisciplinary, collaborative approach and strong commitment from all stakeholders at every level to achieve 'Zero Harm'.

Climate risk (acute physical risks like flooding/drought, and transitional risks such as regulatory/technology/market shifts), water stress affecting operations and communities, and biodiversity impacts from operations on surrounding ecosystems.
Heavy reliance on natural resources such as limestone and coal; ensuring a continuous, cost-effective and quality supply is critical for smooth operations.

Energy expenses constitute a significant portion of production costs, particularly during energy-intensive kilning and grinding processes, making the Company sensitive to energy price inflation and supply disruption.

one-line thesis: Ambuja delivered record annual volume growth of 16% YoY to 73.7M tonnes but faced cost inflation peaking at INR4,500/tonne in Q4 due to acquired asset inefficiencies and supply chain shocks; the company is now prioritizing operational stabilization of Sanghi/Penna assets and green energy/fly ash savings to drive margin recovery in FY27, with volume growth guided at 8% despite soft industry demand.

growth verticals / optionality: 10M tonnes new capacity (GU + clinker) to be commissioned by Sept 2026; Mundra (new clinker line) and Assam limestone block as new greenfield entries; potential for 119M tonnes capacity by FY27; long-term capex deferred to FY30 as focus shifts to optimizing existing assets

themes.title: Cement demand & pricing recovery
themes.need: Q1FY27 turned cement from a pricing story into a volume-share-plus-fuel-cost story. ULTRACEMCO grew domestic grey volume +13.1% YoY against an estimated ~7-8% industry, delivered its first Rs 5,000cr+ April-June EBITDA (Rs 5,146cr) with EBITDA/ton held above Rs 1,200, and crossed 200.1 MT domestic capacity a year early - but guided Q2FY27 cost UP ~Rs 130-140/ton and pinned the Rs 1,400/ton consolidated target to Q4FY28. The fuel shock, not price, is the swing factor: JKCEMENT's EBITDA/ton fell to Rs 982 from Rs 1,229 YoY despite +19% grey volume, DALBHARAT flagged pet coke 'surged to nearly $160/t' versus a pre-war $110-115, and NUVOCO defended INR 1,079/ton EBITDA only by cutting petcoke from 37% to 27% of fuel mix in a single quarter. Consolidation is visibly compounding (INDIACEM EBITDA/ton Rs 386->400->509->603 across four quarters; DALBHARAT closed Jaypee at Rs 2,850cr EV with Chunar operational and Rewa on trial within 50 days) even as DALBHARAT slipped its 75mt milestone from FY27 to FY28. SHREECEM/RAMCOCEM/JKLAKSHMI/JSWCEMENT/STARCEMENT/BIRLACORPN ride the same volume + consolidation axis.
themes.driver: Q2FY27 is the guided cost trough - ULTRACEMCO ~Rs 130-140/ton, JKCEMENT ~Rs 150/ton and BIRLACORPN Rs 70-80/ton of incremental cost; then fuel-mix agility (NUVOCO's petcoke swing) and whether DALBHARAT's ~Rs 150/t of procurement savings is really 'permanent, not timing'.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Cement demand in India expected to grow around 5% in FY 2026-27, following a 6.5-7.5% growth trajectory in FY 2025-26, supported by sustained momentum across housing and infrastructure sectors
- GST reduction on cement, together with the Government's continued focus on infrastructure-led development, expected to further support demand momentum in FY 2026-27
- Per-capita cement consumption in India (~290 kg) remains significantly below the global average (~540 kg), indicating substantial long-term structural headroom for growth
- Rising capital expenditure on highways, ports, metro rail networks and industrial corridors, reinforced by the $2.6 trillion National Infrastructure Pipeline, expected to sustain infrastructure-led demand
- Long-term consumption further supported by PLI schemes, Smart Cities initiatives, sustained FDI inflows and China+1-driven manufacturing shifts
- Industry capacity additions projected at 42-44 MTPA in FY 2026-27 (following 50-55 MTPA in FY 2025-26); capacity utilisation expected to remain stable around 70-71%, higher in northern/central regions and relatively moderate in the south due to capacity overhang
- Elevated input costs (higher coal, petcoke and freight expenses, and rupee depreciation on imported inputs) remain a cost-pressure headwind being actively managed
- Demand improved sequentially in H2 FY 2025-26 versus H1 FY 2025-26 (average growth of 6-6.5%), driven by post-monsoon construction activity acceleration

Specific projects under way include a 1.5 MTPA capacity addition at Sindri (organic route), a 0.3 MTPA addition through debottlenecking, and 3.4 MTPA of ongoing expansion comprising 2.4 MTPA at Salai Banwa and 1 MTPA at Kalamboli. ACC's own standalone cement capacity stood at 40.4 MTPA. Alongside capacity growth, the Company is expanding captive power (315 MW installed capacity, including 86 MW of Waste Heat Recovery Systems) and pursuing rail and sea-based logistics investments (e.g. at Sanghipuram, via captive jetty) to support expansion economics. moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- India's first cement company with ~90 years of industry experience and multi-generational brand trust
- Part of Adani Cement's integrated industrial platform (energy, logistics, infrastructure), converting scale into operational resilience
- Large limestone resource base (10.95 Bn MT for the Adani Cement business) supporting raw-material security
- Extensive distribution reach: 1,20,000+ channel partners and 13,973 dealers/distributors nationally
- Premiumisation strength — 44% share of premium products; recognised 'India's Most Trusted Cement Brand 2025' by TRA Research for the third consecutive year
- Strong credit profile — AAA (Stable) long-term and A1+ short-term ratings from CRISIL and CARE Ratings, on a debt-free balance sheet
- Digital/AI-enabled operations via CiNOC (Cement Intelligent Network Operations Centre) improving reliability, energy optimisation and decision-making

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Accelerate growth through capacity expansion via both greenfield and brownfield routes, targeting 119 MTPA (Adani Cement platform) by FY 2026-27
- Advance the 'One Cement Platform' by integrating ACC and Orient Cement with Ambuja Cements to unify governance, manufacturing, supply chain and capital deployment
- Strengthen and reinforce the iconic ACC brand through channel-partner expansion, IHB/contractor/engineer engagement programmes and brand campaigns
- Lead in ESG standards by conducting business responsibly, sustainably and inclusively while expanding eco-friendly/blended-cement …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Governance] Stated governance pathway includes tenure of Independent Directors up to 3 years for a maximum of 2 terms, minimum 30% female directors, share ownership for the CEO and executive committee members, and independent third-party review and certification of Related Party Transactions.
- [Mergers] Deck discloses completed mergers of Sanghi (w.e.f. 1st April 2024) and Penna (w.e.f. 16th August 2024) into Ambuja, generating tax shields from unabsorbed depreciation and accumulated business losses; "The overall one-time benefit in the consolidated financials for FY26 is approximately Rs 1,365 Cr."
- [Group event] "AEL has raised INR 15,000 Cr through Qualified Institutional Placement ('QIP') during July'26. Accordingly, promoter's shareholding stands revised to 71.97%."
- [Awards] ACC-linked recognitions in Q1 FY'27: "ACC has been recognised among India's Most Sustainable Companies 2026 in the Cement Sector by Business Today", and the Ametha plant received the British Safety Council International Safety Award 2026 (Merit Category), "a recognition that reflects ACC's strong commitment to health, safety and well-being".
- [Related party] Volume reconciliation deducts "Cement Sales (under MSA)" from gross listed-company sales, indicating material inter-company cement sales under a Master Supply Agreement within the platform; the deck does not describe the MSA's terms.
